THE create_node MERGE-VERSUS-REPLACE CONTRADICTION IS ALREADY FIXED ON MAIN AND HAS NEVER BEEN RELEASED. Verified from source and git rather than reasoned about, 2026-08-09.

WHAT WAS REPORTED (dragon Boss cca98fbf, storyflow, v0.26.1): two served surfaces contradict each other on a destructive operation. `create_node`'s tool description says an existing id MERGES; the `revise-design` skill said it is create-or-REPLACE and "resets every other property to its schema default". The reporter observed merging (N=2) and correctly declined to say which surface was authoritative.

GROUND TRUTH, read from the code: the MCP tool calls `upsert_node`, not `create_node` — crates/reflow2-mcp/src/tools/query.rs:64. IT MERGES. The core does expose both semantics (graph.rs:232 create_node replaces, graph.rs:257 upsert_node merges) but no MCP caller can reach the replacing one. THE TOOL DESCRIPTION WAS RIGHT AND THE SKILL WAS WRONG — wrong in the safe direction for data, expensive in effort: it scared agents off the safe call.

⭐ AND THE FIX ALREADY EXISTS. Commit 9b16162 (PR #126, 2026-08-09) rewrote that paragraph, and the corrected text ALREADY CITES THIS FLEET: "It cost a dev_storyflow worker a hand-assembled whole-property write (filed 2026-08-09)." So an earlier report from the same fleet produced the fix, and the fleet then re-filed the same defect because THEY CANNOT SEE MAIN.

⚠️ THE ACTIONABLE FINDING IS THEREFORE NOT THE DEFECT. `git merge-base --is-ancestor 9b16162 v0.26.1` → FALSE, and `git tag --contains 9b16162` → EMPTY. storyflow runs v0.26.1. EIGHT merged PRs sit unreleased on main (#119 #120 #121 #126 #127 #128 #130 #131) and a ninth is open. The trial case for reflow2's governance is evaluating a build that predates every governance fix made in response to it, and is spending real effort re-filing things already repaired.

THIS IS THE SECOND CONFIRMED INSTANCE OF THE SAME PATTERN: a 2026-08-08 review found 2 of 4 storyflow reports had already shipped an hour before they were filed. The gap is DISTRIBUTION, not detection — and rule:fixes-are-judged-by-the-third-party makes it a product problem rather than a repo one, because every consumer is on the same released build the fleet is.

WHAT REMAINS GENUINELY UNFIXED from the report: nothing about create_node. The reporter's wider point stands and is NOT closed by the release — two served surfaces can still disagree, and nothing checks a skill's claims about tool BEHAVIOUR. That is a standing hole with four prior instances.
